name: regions
title: A standing population of regions
caption: Lane D's evolved-turnover-n05-188 (two-shell rule, axis stencil, n0 0.5, g1 −0.5), 128×128×48, t = 300. The photograph is a one-layer slice at mid-depth seen from above, lit by the simulation's own light. The grey shows solid above the region tracker's threshold, (q10+q90)/2 of s, that belongs to the largest connected component. Orange marks every other component; it is a label, not pigment. One connected network holds most of the solid (84% of thresholded voxels at the end). The 980 regions are small fragments on its edges: median 15 voxels, spanning about 4 of 48 layers. Most are broken stripe segments lying along the local stripe direction, crowded where stripe grains meet. They are born, die, split and merge: over the second half, 227 births, 450 deaths, 806 splits and 464 merges, 0.014 events per region per unit time. This is the first standing population of regions the substrate has produced. It is not a claim about life. The film is diagnostic, not lit. It is made from lane D's solid-only captures every 2 time units and shows an 8-layer mid-depth slab with the same colours. Between t ≈ 60 and 150 the network opens up and fragments appear along the openings. After that the fragment field changes slowly, mostly as flicker at fragment edges.

name: regions-3d
title: Regions, lower half
caption: The same state with the upper half of the slab removed, seen at an angle. Orange marks fragments as above (a label, not pigment). Through the depth, the fragments sit in the gaps and seams of the herringbone network.

name: iso-labyrinth
title: Labyrinth
caption: Recipe iso-20261016-06 (tied two-shell rule on the isotropic 19-point stencil, predicted Turing at 6.3 cells), 128×128×48, run 10× its 8-e-fold length (2060 steps). The photograph is a 5-cell horizontal slice at mid-depth seen from above, lit by the simulation's light, with camera density 6. Solid forms a labyrinth that straightens into stripe domains. Measured s wavelength 6.7 cells (7.5 at recipe length). The orientation is not random: the stripes favour the two lattice diagonals. Power on the dominant ring is 8× higher at its strongest angle than its weakest (8 bins), against ~200× for the axis stencil, and other world seeds pick the same diagonals. The film shows the slice from noise to a pigmented labyrinth to straightening stripes.

name: iso-spots
title: Spots and stripes
caption: iso-20261016-02, 1600 steps (10×), the same mid-depth slice. Spots and short stripes mix, with no preferred direction (angular max/min 1.65). Wavelength 7.5 cells against 6.3 predicted. Contrast peaks early (std_s 0.14 at step 320) and then softens (0.065) while solid saturates near 0.35 and waste rises to 0.10.

name: iso-columns-below
title: Columns, from inside
caption: iso-02 again, the camera inside the slab near the floor looking up toward the lit top. The spots of the plan view are columns running the full 48-cell depth. Their bases are dim and their tops are bright in the material's own light, with pigment threads between them.

name: iso-labyrinth-oblique
title: Labyrinth, whole slab
caption: iso-06 seen whole from above at an angle. In depth the labyrinth walls are vertical sheets, so the side faces show the pattern as columns.

name: iso-labyrinth-section
title: Labyrinth, cut
caption: iso-06 cut on a vertical diagonal. The labyrinth walls are vertical sheets running the full 48-cell depth.

name: lamellae
title: Lamellae
caption: Analysis-lane recipe tied-20261016-10 (two-shell rule, predicted Turing at 6.6 cells), 128×128×48, alpha_s 0.05, alpha_p 0.1, dt 0.0055, run 6× its 8-e-fold length (5442 steps). Solid organizes into sheets that go through the whole depth. The sheets form grains of x-oriented and y-oriented stripes, because the second shell couples only along the axes. Measured s wavelength 6.9 cells (FFT centroid) against 6.6 predicted. Contrast saturates (std_s 0.155 at the recipe's end, 0.233 at 6×) while mean s creeps from 0.16 to 0.34 and waste accumulates. The film is the same run: a uniform pigmented skin breaks into a labyrinth, which coarsens into grains.

name: lamellae-section
title: Lamellae, cut
caption: The same specimen cut on a vertical diagonal. Lit only by its own light, the sheets read as diagonal bands on the cut face and dim with depth.

name: crossgrain
title: Cross-grain
caption: tied-20261016-09 (predicted 7.05 cells, measured 7.26), 13476 steps (6× recipe). Same mosaic of orthogonal stripe grains. Here the pattern keeps sharpening after it forms (std_s 0.10 → 0.20) while erosion slowly converts solid to waste (mean s 0.37 → 0.29, w 0.04 → 0.18).

name: lamellae-sheet
title: Lamellae in a sheet
caption: tied-20261016-10 in a 16-cell-thick sheet instead of 48. Same wavelength (6.9) and the same grain mosaic: the pattern is set by the activity rule, not by depth or by the light gradient. A run with L_ambient 0.3 and L0 0.7 (weaker vertical gradient) also gave 6.9 cells and std_s 0.24, with no visible difference except a brighter interior.

name: veined-floor
title: Veined floor
caption: Atlas rule turing-04 at translucent optics (alpha_s 0.05, alpha_p 0.02), 128³, 20000 steps. The bottom 15 layers, lit only by the 3% of light that reaches them. Activity settled into single-cell alternating domains; pigment collects where domains meet, so the walls between chambers are drawn in pigment. The structure is fixed by step ~8000. The film is a fresh run of the same recipe to step 4000, the front quarter cut away: a pigment tide sinks and leaves the veins behind.

name: strata-section
title: Strata, same specimen
caption: The veined-floor run cut on a vertical diagonal: a bright crust, a band of pigment blotches under it, a clearer middle layer, and the vein network in the dim bottom. Pigment is shown above 0.6 with a camera-only stain.

name: receding-front
title: Receding front
caption: turing-04 again with the newer defaults (alpha_s 0.05, alpha_p 0.1), 8000 steps. Solid fills only the upper half and ends in a lobed front. Below it, the dark lower half holds uniform pigment (0.99) and no solid. Exposure 16 to see the front at L ≈ 0.01.

name: crust-underside
title: Crust from beneath
caption: Atlas turing-06 at alpha_s 0.05, alpha_p 0.1, 4000 steps. All the solid is in a 12-layer crust; below it nutrient stays at 0.5, unspent, because nothing deposits there. The camera sits in that empty lower half and looks up at the crust's pigmented, nodular underside, lit by the light that got through.

name: lit-skin
title: Lit skin (original optics)
caption: Atlas turing-02 with the original alpha 2.0 per cell, 3000 steps. Light dies within a few layers, so the material is a bright crust about eight layers down. Under it, columns of transmitted light make streaks, and below that the slab is dark waste. This is the regime the translucent defaults replaced.
